cf.title: Separate catalog_xmin from xmin in walsender hot standby feedback

input.subject: Separate catalog_xmin from xmin in walsender hot standby feedback

verdict_reasoning: The problem is real: the code comment admits it, and Amit Kapila engaged with it in message #3. The thread does not say why wal_receiver_create_temp_slot on the standby is not enough (already-exists-1). The ephemeral-slot version also changes WAL retention and max_replication_slots use for every slotless feedback standby, while only standbys with an older catalog_xmin gain (demand-2). No report from a production system is shown (demand-1).

brief.title: Track catalog_xmin separately from xmin for walsenders without a slot
brief.problem: Without a physical replication slot, the walsender stores min(xmin, catalog_xmin) from hot standby feedback in its PGPROC xmin. An old catalog_xmin from a logical slot on the standby then holds back vacuum of all user tables on the primary. The author targets HA setups that avoid physical slots and use wal_keep_size or archiving instead.
brief.proposed_design: v1/v2 add a catalog_xmin field to PGPROC that ComputeXidHorizons() applies only to the catalog and shared horizons, and GetReplicationHorizons() passes upstream for cascading. After review, the author switched to having the walsender create an ephemeral physical slot (pg_walsender_<pid>) on first feedback and track both horizons through it. If max_replication_slots is full, it falls back to today's min() behavior.
user_visible_surface: A physical slot named pg_walsender_<pid> appears in pg_replication_slots for each slotless feedback standby while it is connected, with temporary = 'f'.
The new slot pins WAL through restart_lsn, bounded by max_slot_wal_keep_size.
Slotless feedback walsenders now use up entries of max_replication_slots.
C API: ReplicationSlotCreate gets a new error_if_full argument.
author_claims: The data horizon is no longer held back by a standby's catalog_xmin, while catalog protection stays in place.
The PGPROC version showed no measurable pgbench cost on a 104-core machine; the patched build was 1.3% to 1.9% faster, which the author calls noise.
The ephemeral slot avoids the extra 4 bytes per PGPROC and updates both horizons together under the slot mutex.
Pinning WAL for a connected standby is desirable, and the slot drops when the walsender exits.
No replication connection breaks, because a full slot pool falls back to the current behavior.
brief.thread_state: Amit Kapila objected to the PGPROC version (4 bytes per process, a possible torn read of xmin and catalog_xmin) and suggested ephemeral slots. The author posted an ephemeral-slot prototype; nobody has replied to it, the last message is truncated, and CFbot reports the patch needs a rebase.
unclear: The ephemeral-slot patch lists no TAP test and no documentation changes.
The material does not say whether the new WAL retention for slotless standbys can be turned off, or how it interacts with wal_keep_size setups that avoid slots on purpose.
The proposal does not say what happens to the slot name or slot reuse when the walsender pid is reused.
The material does not say why repack_worker.c, launcher.c and slotsync.c change beyond the new ReplicationSlotCreate argument.
The ephemeral-slot version has no performance numbers, and the material does not say whether it changes the walsender restart_lsn when no feedback is sent.
The message truncation hides the rest of the author's recommendation.

objections.title: wal_receiver_create_temp_slot already gives slotless standbys a separate catalog_xmin
objections.failure_scenario: An HA operator who avoids permanent slots can already set wal_receiver_create_temp_slot = on on the standby. The walreceiver then creates a temporary physical slot, and the primary tracks xmin and catalog_xmin separately through that slot, which drops on disconnect. The patch adds a second, server-side mechanism for the same job.
objections.argument: Message #1 lists the slot downsides as lost slots after failover, re-creating slots on the new primary, and dangling slots. A temporary slot created by the walreceiver avoids all three: the standby creates it on each new upstream, and the upstream drops it at disconnect. The ephemeral-slot version in message #4 is close to this existing feature, but primary-side and with temporary = 'f'. The thread does not mention the existing setting or say why it is not enough.
objections.author_must_show: What does a primary-created pg_walsender_<pid> slot do that a standby with wal_receiver_create_temp_slot = on cannot do today?

critic.reasoning: wal_receiver_create_temp_slot exists and the thread does not discuss it, so the objection stands. It is fixable, because the code comment and Amit Kapila both point to this direction, and the PGPROC version splits the horizons without any slot.

objections.title: All slotless feedback standbys pay for a fix few of them need
objections.failure_scenario: A DBA runs standbys without slots on purpose and relies on wal_keep_size. After an upgrade, every walsender with feedback creates pg_walsender_<pid>. A lagging standby now pins WAL, and with the default max_slot_wal_keep_size = -1 the primary disk can fill. Slot-count monitoring also starts alerting on slots with temporary = 'f'.
objections.argument: Only standbys that host a logical slot gain from the change. The ephemeral-slot version still changes WAL retention and max_replication_slots use for every slotless standby that sends feedback, and the material shows no way to turn it off. Message #4 calls the WAL pinning 'a feature', but these users chose to avoid slots for this reason, as message #1 itself says. The claimed bound depends on max_slot_wal_keep_size, which is unlimited by default.
objections.author_must_show: Can the slot be created only when feedback carries a catalog_xmin different from xmin, and how do sites that use wal_keep_size keep today's WAL retention?

critic.reasoning: The scenario overlaps replication-ondisk-1, but the point is separate. The slot is created on first feedback for every slotless standby, and only standbys that report an older catalog_xmin gain from it.

objections.title: No field evidence that the affected group is more than a narrow case
objections.failure_scenario: A committer accepts a new walsender slot lifecycle and a changed ReplicationSlotCreate API. The bug only bites setups that combine a slotless physical standby, hot_standby_feedback, and a logical slot on that standby with an old catalog_xmin. If few sites run that combination, the project carries the code and its edge cases for little gain.
objections.argument: Message #1 asserts that 'many production HA deployments' avoid physical slots and points to 'Patroni with certain configurations', but it gives no bug report, -general thread or bloat numbers from a real system. Nobody besides the author asks for the fix in the thread. The only validation in message #4 shows the horizons differing by one xid on a test pair. A workaround also exists: give that one standby a physical slot, bounded by max_slot_wal_keep_size.
objections.author_must_show: Which production systems hit this combination, how much bloat did it cause, and why was a physical slot for that standby not an acceptable fix for them?

critic.reasoning: The thread has no report from a second user and no bloat numbers from a real system. The code comment admits the limitation, which supports that the problem exists but does not show how many sites hit it.

other_surviving.title: Implicit slots take max_replication_slots entries from user-created slots
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A primary has max_replication_slots sized for its logical subscriptions plus a few spare entries. Several slotless feedback standbys connect and each takes an entry. Then create subscription or pg_create_physical_replication_slot() fails with "all replication slots are in use", and the DBA cannot see why from configuration alone.
other_surviving.argument: In message #4, error_if_full = false protects only the walsender. Every other caller keeps the old erroring behaviour and now competes with slots that the server creates on its own. So existing capacity planning for max_replication_slots stops being correct after upgrade without any configuration change. The proposal does not say whether these slots are reserved or counted separately, or whether this change is documented as an upgrade note.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Should server-created walsender slots count against max_replication_slots, and how would a user-created logical or physical slot be guaranteed an entry?

critic.reasoning: Message #4 confirms the walsender slots use max_replication_slots entries, and error_if_full protects only the walsender. Other slot creators still get an error, and the setting needs a restart to raise.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Ephemeral slot adds WAL retention that slotless standbys chose to avoid
other_surviving.failure_scenario: An HA setup runs a slotless standby with wal_keep_size and the default max_slot_wal_keep_size = -1. The standby stays connected but falls far behind. The new pg_walsender_<pid> slot's restart_lsn pins WAL with no limit, and pg_wal fills the primary's disk.
other_surviving.argument: Message #1 describes users who avoid slots on purpose because slots retain WAL. Message #4 calls pinning "a feature" and says max_slot_wal_keep_size bounds it, but the default is unlimited, so the bound is opt-in. wal_sender_timeout only covers dead standbys, not slow ones that are still connected. The proposal changes WAL retention for every slotless feedback standby on upgrade, and it gives no way to turn this off.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Can the ephemeral slot track xmin and catalog_xmin while leaving restart_lsn invalid, or what opt-out keeps today's WAL retention for slotless standbys?

critic.reasoning: Message #4 confirms that restart_lsn pins WAL while the standby is connected, and max_slot_wal_keep_size is -1 by default. wal_sender_timeout does not cover a standby that replies but receives slowly, and the material shows no opt-out.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Long-lived RS_EPHEMERAL slot with a pid-based name stretches slot semantics
other_surviving.failure_scenario: An HA tool or monitoring script sees pg_walsender_<pid> with temporary = 'f' and tries to drop it as an unknown slot, or a user has a slot with that name. A drop of the active slot fails and logs errors. A name collision makes ReplicationSlotCreate raise an error that error_if_full does not catch.
other_surviving.argument: RS_EPHEMERAL is today a short state during slot creation, and the patch now keeps it for a whole connection. Message #4 agrees that temporary = 'f' misleads readers. The proposal does not say how a name collision is handled or whether the pg_walsender_ prefix is reserved, and the patch adds no tests or docs for these cases.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Why not use RS_TEMPORARY or a reserved slot name, and what happens when pg_walsender_<pid> already exists when feedback first arrives?

critic.reasoning: Message #4 weighs the temporary = 'f' display but does not cover a name collision. A user slot named pg_walsender_<pid> makes ReplicationSlotCreate raise an error that error_if_full does not catch, which contradicts the claim that no connection breaks.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Best-effort fallback makes the vacuum horizon depend on slot pool state
other_surviving.failure_scenario: After a restart, standbys reconnect in a different order and one of them finds the slot pool full. That standby silently falls back to min(xmin, catalog_xmin), and user-table bloat returns on the primary. The DBA sees no slot and no message that explains why vacuum stopped cleaning.
other_surviving.argument: Message #4 describes the split as best-effort, with a silent fallback to today's behavior. Message #1 says the bug is already hard to diagnose, and a split that applies only sometimes makes it harder. Nothing in the proposal reports which path a walsender took, and nothing fails loudly when the fallback hides the fix.
other_surviving.author_must_show: How does a DBA see that a given walsender fell back to the combined horizon, for example through a log message or a column in pg_stat_replication?

critic.reasoning: Message #4 calls the split best-effort and describes no log message or view column for the fallback. The fallback is no worse than today, but the only sign of it is a missing row in pg_replication_slots.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

refuted.title: Slotless standbys start pinning WAL with no way to opt out
refuted.failure_scenario: A site runs slotless standbys with wal_keep_size precisely so the primary never retains unbounded WAL. After upgrade, a connected but slow standby with hot_standby_feedback gets a pg_walsender_<pid> slot whose restart_lsn pins WAL. With the default max_slot_wal_keep_size = -1, pg_wal grows until the primary runs out of disk.
refuted.argument: Message #1 says these deployments avoid slots on purpose, and message #4 calls the new WAL pinning "a feature, not a regression". The bound named in message #4 is max_slot_wal_keep_size, which is unlimited by default, and wal_sender_timeout only covers dead standbys, not slow ones that are still connected. The proposal gives an operator no way to keep today's retention contract while also getting the horizon split, and the patch has no documentation hunk for the change.
refuted.author_must_show: How does an operator who uses slotless standbys to avoid WAL pinning keep that behaviour after upgrade, and what limits retention when max_slot_wal_keep_size is left at -1?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1. That one states the same WAL retention scenario and asks the more useful question about leaving restart_lsn invalid.

refuted.title: New slots look persistent and share the user slot namespace
refuted.failure_scenario: An HA tool or monitoring script that reconciles pg_replication_slots against its own list sees pg_walsender_<pid> with temporary = 'f' and alerts on it, or tries to drop it. A user slot that already has a matching name stops the walsender from creating its own slot, and the material does not say what then happens.
refuted.argument: Message #4 says the rows look like "an ordinary persistent physical slot distinguished only by its name prefix". Postgres already has a temporary slot concept with a visible flag, but this proposal adds a third, ephemeral kind that shows up as non-temporary. The proposal does not reserve the pg_walsender_ prefix. It also does not handle a name collision or pid reuse, and the error_if_full path covers a full slot pool only.
refuted.author_must_show: How will pg_replication_slots tell clients that a slot is server-managed and dropped on disconnect, and what happens when the pg_walsender_<pid> name already exists?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-3, which names the error a name collision raises. The pid reuse part is not a failure, because the slot drops when the walsender exits.

refuted.title: Transient walsender slots can block real slot creation
refuted.failure_scenario: A primary sizes max_replication_slots for its logical subscriptions, and several slotless standbys also connect with feedback. Their pg_walsender_<pid> slots fill the pool. A new create subscription or pg_create_physical_replication_slot() then fails with "all replication slots are in use" until a standby disconnects.
refuted.argument: Message #4 handles only the walsender side of exhaustion: the walsender falls back to the min() behavior. The other side is not covered. A slot taken first by a walsender wins over a slot an operator or a subscription asks for later. Users who never set aside slots for these standbys hit a new failure after a minor configuration change or an upgrade.
refuted.author_must_show: How does the design stop implicit walsender slots from taking max_replication_slots entries that users and logical replication need for persistent slots?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2, which describes the same full slot pool and also asks whether the server-created slots should be counted separately.

refuted.title: Slotless feedback standbys now pin WAL with no cap by default
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator runs a slotless standby with hot_standby_feedback = on and caps WAL with wal_keep_size, leaving max_slot_wal_keep_size at its default of -1. The standby stalls on replay but keeps answering keepalives, so the walsender never times out. The ephemeral slot's restart_lsn holds WAL until pg_wal fills and the primary stops.
refuted.argument: Message #4 says the retention is bounded by max_slot_wal_keep_size and wal_sender_timeout. The first bound is unlimited by default, and the second only applies to a standby that stops replying, not to one that lags. Message #1 says these setups avoid slots on purpose so that WAL accumulation stays bounded. Today such a standby falls behind and reconnects from the archive, but under the patch any REPLICATION connection that sends feedback can grow WAL without limit, and the proposal gives no way to turn this off.
refuted.author_must_show: What bounds WAL retention for a slotless feedback standby when max_slot_wal_keep_size is -1, and how can an operator turn the slot off?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1. Its scenario is also weaker: a physical slot's restart_lsn follows the standby's flush position, so a replay stall alone does not pin WAL.

refuted.title: Implicit slot adds WAL retention to setups that avoid slots on purpose
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator runs a slotless standby with wal_keep_size and hot_standby_feedback = on. The standby stays connected but receives WAL slowly, so the implicit slot's restart_lsn holds WAL on the primary. With the default max_slot_wal_keep_size = -1, pg_wal grows until the disk fills, and the operator finds out only when the primary stops.
refuted.argument: Message #1 says these deployments avoid slots partly because slots can cause unbounded WAL accumulation. Message #4 calls the new pinning a feature and says it is bounded by max_slot_wal_keep_size, but that setting is unlimited by default. The proposal gives no way to keep today's retention behavior. A fix for vacuum horizons now also changes WAL disk usage for every slotless feedback standby.
refuted.author_must_show: How can a slotless feedback standby keep today's WAL retention, and what bounds pg_wal growth when max_slot_wal_keep_size is left at its default?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1. It gives the same scenario, the same default of max_slot_wal_keep_size = -1 and the same missing opt-out.

refuted.title: Walsenders take max_replication_slots entries that other features need
refuted.failure_scenario: A primary has max_replication_slots sized for its logical subscriptions. Several slotless feedback standbys connect and each takes a pg_walsender_<pid> slot. A later create subscription or pg_create_logical_replication_slot fails with all slots in use, and the cause is not visible from the error.
refuted.argument: Message #4 handles a full pool for the walsender only: the walsender falls back, while other slot creators still get an error. The cost lands on users of logical replication and slot sync who never asked for this feature. Upgrading users would have to raise max_replication_slots, which needs a restart, and the proposal does not document this.
refuted.author_must_show: Should these slots come from a separate pool, and if not, how does an operator learn that walsenders took the slots a logical subscription now needs?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2. Its point that raising max_replication_slots needs a restart is correct and belongs with that objection.

refuted.title: Long-lived ephemeral slots shown as non-temporary, with a reserved name
refuted.failure_scenario: An HA tool or a monitoring check lists pg_replication_slots, sees a physical slot with temporary = 'f' that it did not create, and alerts on it or tries to drop it. Separately, a user who already has a slot named pg_walsender_1234 can block or confuse slot creation for a walsender that gets that pid.
refuted.argument: Message #4 says the slot looks like an ordinary persistent slot and is distinguished only by its name prefix. RS_EPHEMERAL now covers a slot that lives for a whole connection, which is a new meaning for that state. The proposal does not reserve the name prefix, does not handle pid reuse, and does not say how slotsync.c and failover tooling should treat these slots.
refuted.author_must_show: Will these slots be marked distinctly in pg_replication_slots, and how are name collisions with user slots and reuse of a pid prevented?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-3. The pid reuse part is not a failure, because the slot drops when the walsender exits.

refuted.title: Implicit slots override deployments that avoid slots on purpose
refuted.failure_scenario: A site uses wal_keep_size and archiving, and it chose not to use slots. After an upgrade, every slotless feedback standby gets a pg_walsender_<pid> slot that pins WAL. Those slots also take entries of max_replication_slots, so a planned logical slot can fail to create. The operator finds out from disk usage or a slot creation error.
refuted.argument: The existing opt-in setting leaves this choice to the operator. The proposal makes it automatic and gives no way to turn it off. The users in message #1 avoid slots for this reason. Message #4 calls the WAL pinning "a feature, not a regression". But a lagging standby can then hold WAL up to max_slot_wal_keep_size, which is unlimited by default, where wal_keep_size used to cap it.
refuted.author_must_show: Why should slotless standbys get WAL-pinning slots by default, when wal_receiver_create_temp_slot already lets each standby opt in?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1 for WAL retention and of standards-compat-2 for the slot pool. The comparison with the opt-in setting is already in already-exists-1.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The walsender creates a physical slot whose restart_lsn pins WAL, and hot standby feedback handling changes.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: ReplicationSlotCreate gets a new error_if_full argument; the earlier version added a field to PGPROC.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: Message #1 calls it a fix for a long-standing issue, but it changes a C API and WAL retention.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: A new long-lived use of ephemeral slots in the walsender, with a fallback path when the slot pool is full.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The PGPROC version adds a read per PGPROC in ComputeXidHorizons(); the slot version has no numbers.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: wal_receiver_create_temp_slot already lets a slotless standby get a temporary physical slot that tracks both horizons.

questions: What does a primary-created pg_walsender_<pid> slot do that a standby with wal_receiver_create_temp_slot = on cannot do today?
Can the slot be created only when feedback carries a catalog_xmin older than xmin, so that other slotless standbys see no change?
Can the slot track xmin and catalog_xmin with restart_lsn left invalid, so that wal_keep_size setups keep today's WAL retention?
Which production systems hit this combination, how much bloat did it cause, and why was a physical slot for that standby not acceptable?
Should server-created walsender slots count against max_replication_slots, and what happens when a slot named pg_walsender_<pid> already exists?

committability.owner_note: Amit Kapila reviewed the PGPROC version in message #3 and suggested ephemeral slots; nobody has replied to the ephemeral-slot prototype. The owner needs to know replication slots and the xid horizon code.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the walsender slot lifecycle, the changed WAL retention for slotless standbys, and the correctness of the catalog horizon, with no end date.
committability.author_follow_up: The author rebased, added measurements, wrote a new prototype after review in message #3, and moved the entry across three CommitFests.

priority.reason: Only slotless feedback standbys that host a logical slot gain, but the slot version changes behavior for every slotless feedback standby. The patch is small but touches slot, walsender and horizon code, and the choice between PGPROC, an implicit slot and the existing standby setting is open.

provisional_note: The code was not read, and the text of message #4 is not in the material. Whether restart_lsn must be set, how a name collision behaves, and why repack_worker.c, launcher.c and slotsync.c change could not be checked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Reuse Workers and Replication Slots during Logical Replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets a tablesync worker, after it finishes one table, pick up the next table in init state and sync it, keeping its replication slot. This removes the cost of starting a new worker and creating and dropping a slot for each table, which matters most for many empty or small tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Benchmarks by reviewers showed regressions in some settings, and the v28 design #2 results were up to about twice as slow as HEAD and varied widely between runs. The patch also no longer applied to HEAD. Amit Kapila proposed Returned with feedback because the regressions still needed analysis, and vignesh C asked for a new entry with a fix for the regression.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
IIRC, there were some regressions observed with this patch. So, one
needs to analyze those as well.

precedents_retrieved.title: Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
Reverted commit(s): Track conflict_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Till now, the reason for replication slot invalidation is not tracked
directly in pg_replication_slots. A recent commit 007693f2a3 added
'conflict_reason' to show the reasons for slot conflict/invalidation, but
only for logical slots.

This commit adds a new column 'invalidation_reason' to show invalidation
reasons for both physical and logical slots. And, this commit also turns
'conflict_reason' text column to 'conflicting' boolean column (effectively
reverting commit 007693f2a3). The 'conflicting' column is true for
invalidation reasons 'rows_removed' and 'wal_level_insufficient' because
those make the slot conflict with recovery. When 'conflicting' is true,
one can now look at the new 'invalidation_reason' column for the reason
for the logical slot's conflict with recovery.

The new 'invalidation_reason' column will also be useful to track other
invalidation reasons in the future commit.

precedents_retrieved.title: Synchronize logical replication slots from primary to standby
precedents_retrieved.summary: A background worker on a physical standby periodically fetches logical replication slot information from the primary, so that after failover a logical subscriber finds up-to-date slots on the new primary. Later versions added synchronize_slot_names on the standby to pick which slots to sync, and standby_slot_names on the primary to hold logical replication back until the listed physical standbys catch up.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund found that the patch breaks the catalog_xmin guarantee: row versions still needed for logical decoding on the standby can be removed. He said it needs a mechanism such as the "Minimal logical decoding on standbys" patch, which the author said was not near ready. Reviewers also objected to the blocking wait and the per-commit work added to reorderbuffer.c, and to the worker-per-database design tied to the logical replication launcher. The author listed these and an open configuration design as significant jobs still to do.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The patch as-is just breaks one of the fundamental guarantees necessary for logical decoding, that no rows versions can be removed that are still required for logical decoding (signalled via catalog_xmin).

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add test case for obsoleting slot with active walsender"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add test case for obsoleting slot with active walsender"
Reverted commit(s): Add test case for obsoleting slot with active walsender
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 09126984a263; the test case added there failed once
in circumstances that remain mysterious.  It seems better to remove the
test for now so that 14beta2 doesn't have random failures built in.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix cancelled queries when hot_standby_feedback = on
precedents_retrieved.summary: With hot_standby_feedback = on, standby queries still get cancelled when vacuum truncates a heap on the primary, because the AccessExclusiveLock taken for truncation is replayed on the standby. The final patch adds a new lock level, ACCESS EXCLUSIVE LOCAL, that vacuum uses for heap truncation and that is not WAL-logged, so standby queries must tolerate concurrent truncation.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane showed that letting scans run during truncation leaves a race: concurrent scans can load to-be-truncated pages back into shared buffers before ftruncate, and reading past EOF on a standby can extend the relation. Alexander Korotkov agreed the patch had to be revised and sketched a new truncation design, but Robert Haas called it fragile and doubted it prevents stale buffers from being taken as valid. No new version followed, the existing patch failed initdb, and the entry was closed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: If we ever have valid-looking buffers in shared_buffers after the corresponding data has been truncated away on disk, we've got to make sure that nobody ever confuses one of them with an actually-valid buffer.

precedents_retrieved.title: Error "initial slot snapshot too large" in create replication slot
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes the "initial slot snapshot too large" error in CREATE_REPLICATION_SLOT, which happens because SnapBuildInitialSnapshot puts top-level and subtransaction XIDs into the xip array and the count can exceed GetMaxSnapshotXidCount(). Versions tried excluding subtransactions, marking the snapshot takenDuringRecovery, asking the reorder buffer which XIDs are subtransactions, and finally using the subxip array as an extension of xip.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas objected to the last version because it adds a third way of using the xip and subxip arrays, and he saw no consensus on an approach. Earlier approaches failed for other reasons: the reorder buffer cannot reliably tell subtransactions apart, using takenDuringRecovery was rejected, and resizing xip made procarray.c and snapmgr.c too complicated. The author withdrew the entry for lack of a simple fix.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It's bad enough that we
already use the xip/subxip arrays in two different ways depending on
the situation. Increasing that to three different ways seems painful.

precedents_retrieved.title: Replica sends an incorrect epoch in its hot standby feedback to the Master
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes a bug in Postgres 9.6, 10 and 11 where a replica's nextXid can move backward during WAL replay in RecordKnownAssignedTransactionIds, so hot standby feedback carries a wrong epoch and the master ignores the replica's xmin. The one-line fix advances nextXid only when the new value is higher, as similar code elsewhere does.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The withdrawal was not a rejection of the fix. The author registered the patch in the commitfest more than once, and David Steele marked the duplicate entries 2462 and 2463 as withdrawn. The visible messages show no objection, and Thomas Munro agreed the nextXid assignment looked wrong.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I have marked the duplicate entries 2462 and 2463 as withdrawn.

precedents_retrieved.title: Forbid the use of invalidated physical slots in streaming replication.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes StartReplication() reject a physical replication slot that has already been invalidated, for example by max_slot_wal_keep_size, as the logical walsender already does. Without it a walsender can stream from an invalidated slot, move its restart_lsn forward, and pg_replication_slots shows it as valid while it protects neither WAL nor rows.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding to review questions, so vignesh C moved the entry to Waiting on Author and then to Returned with Feedback. Ashutosh Bapat asked how a build before commit 15f8203 behaves and warned that changing long-released behaviour of physical slots could break backward compatibility. Robert Haas noted that the documentation does not match the current behaviour and that the intended interaction with physical slots is not clear.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think making logical and physical slot behaviour consistent would be
better but if the inconsistent behaviour is out there for some
releases, changing that now will break backward compatibility.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert changes to CONCURRENTLY that "sped up" Xmin advance
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert changes to CONCURRENTLY that "sped up" Xmin advance
Reverted commit(s): VACUUM: ignore indexing operations with CONCURRENTLY
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit d9d076222f5b "VACUUM: ignore indexing operations
with CONCURRENTLY".

These changes caused indexes created with the CONCURRENTLY option to
miss heap tuples that were HOT-updated and HOT-pruned during the index
creation.  Before these changes, HOT pruning would have been prevented
by the Xmin of the transaction creating the index, but because this
change was precisely to allow the Xmin to move forward ignoring that
backend, now other backends scanning the table can prune them.  This is
not a problem for VACUUM (which requires a lock that conflicts with a
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY operation), but HOT-prune can definitely
occur.  In other words, Xmin advancement was sped up, but at the cost of
corrupting the resulting index.

Regrettably, this means that the new feature in PG14 that RIC/CIC on
very large tables no longer force VACUUM to retain very old tuples goes
away.  We might try to implement it again in a later release, but for
now the risk of indexes missing tuples is too high and there's no easy
fix.

Backpatch to 14, where this change appeared.

precedents_retrieved.title: Exit walsender before confirming remote flush in logical replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets a logical replication walsender exit at shutdown without waiting for the subscriber to confirm flush of all sent WAL, so that a publisher with a large time-delayed apply can still stop. Later versions add an optional SHUTDOWN_MODE clause ('wait_flush' or 'immediate') to START_REPLICATION for logical replication.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last shown messages, about a month before the decision, still discuss whether the option should be a boolean or a mode with an explicit default, and they contain minor review comments on v7-0002.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This partially reverts 096bbf7 and 9d2d457, undoing the libpq changes as
it could cause breakages in distributions that share one single libpq
version across multiple major versions of Postgres for extensions and
applications linking to that.

Note that the backend is unchanged here, and it still disables SSL
compression while simplifying the underlying catalogs that tracked if
compression was enabled or not for a SSL connection.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found for this idea. [P9] is a revert because a held xmin was ignored and HOT pruning then broke CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY; here the catalog horizon stays held, and slots already split the two horizons this way, so that reason does not carry over. [P3] failed because it broke the catalog_xmin guarantee, which this proposal keeps. The only earlier trace in the thread is the XXX comment in ProcessStandbyHSFeedbackMessage() about ephemeral slots (messages #1, #2, #4). The thread reports no earlier discussion or rejection of that comment's idea.
Objections listed above. Neither precedent applies to the user-facing contract this angle covers.

The PGPROC version (messages #1 and #2) is superseded, so the objections address the ephemeral-slot design in message #4. Message #4 is truncated, so later parts of its recommendation could not be checked.

The patch adds no new privilege. A REPLICATION role could already create slots, so using up max_replication_slots or pinning WAL is not an escalation, and the objection above is about the safe default. Possible slot name collisions with pg_walsender_<pid> could not be checked without the code.
The four objections above cover the ephemeral-slot design. No committer has reviewed that design yet, and only Amit Kapila commented on the earlier one.
